description: Durably retain Workflow turn events and follow-up user input on the originating runner, retry them in AgentSession order across network failure and runner restart, and keep delivery independent of runtime execution.

tasks.title: Deliver Workflow AgentSession events durably
tasks.description: Implement the shared runner-local `AgentSessionRuntimeEventOutbox` with durable snapshot storage, explicit acknowledgement policies, per-AgentSession FIFO delivery, independent cross-session progress, and complete startup/reconnect/stop lifecycle. Wire Workflow OpenCode input, projected activity, and terminal close reporting through that outbox so local persistence settles without waiting for Server delivery and the runtime result remains authoritative.
acceptanceCriteria: The shared outbox durably records one-event entries containing a local record ID, binding-free Workflow or generic Session target, original `runtimeSessionId`, optional work metadata, payload, and stable sequence position before starting delivery; the physical snapshot uses atomic replacement and owner-only permissions under `.mohist/runner-state/runtime-events.json`.

The real snapshot/import store depends on an injected `RuntimeEventOutboxFileSystem`; tests run that store against a recording in-memory implementation and verify serialization, owner-only write options, temporary-write/rename ordering, restart reload, and failure boundaries without instantiating the Node filesystem adapter or touching a temporary directory.

Workflow and generic content-event delivery each send exactly one queue head per request and remove a `matching-receipt` record only when `AgentSessionRuntimeEventReceipt[]` contains the submitted type; timeout, transport failure, non-2xx, malformed or empty response, and a receipt without that type retain the head for retry.

`ServerConnection.agentSessionRuntimeEvents` returns and validates the receipt array already produced by the generic Server route, while the existing Workflow method retains the same response contract; no Server endpoint, request DTO, persistence model, deduplication behavior, or external dependency changes.

The outbox preserves FIFO order by canonical logical Session target, allows at most one in-flight head per Session, prevents input/activity/close overtaking across reused turns or bindings, never retargets a stale event, and drains other Session queues with bounded concurrency when one head remains unaccepted.

Runner startup loads the outbox before accepting commands or claiming work, kicks initial delivery without awaiting a full drain, and resumes pending work after automatic or forced reconnect; stop cancels retry timers and HTTP attempts without deleting records, and an unavailable/corrupt store prevents new work from silently falling back to best-effort upload.

Focused RunnerHost specs prove an unhealthy outbox prevents polling/claiming even when OpenCode is ready, an outbox that becomes unhealthy stops later claims, and restored health resumes claiming while already-running work and pending delivery retain their specified behavior.

`WorkflowAgentSessionReporter` no longer performs direct HTTP uploads: it awaits durable enqueue of the composed `session.input` before prompt execution, immediately registers ordered enqueue promises for normalized live and reconciled events, records one logical completed/failed `session.closed` after runtime completion, and waits for all local writes to settle before returning without waiting for Server acceptance.

A process exit before an observed event's asynchronous local enqueue commits is explicitly outside restart recovery; focused coverage instead proves that every completed local enqueue survives a reconstructed outbox and that the Workflow result cannot return while its local event writes remain unsettled.

A completed, failed, interrupted, or timed-out Workflow turn returns the original OpenCode result without waiting for event acceptance; terminal status and failure reason remain derived from that runtime result, and event retries never invoke the OpenCode prompt again.

Focused Workflow specs prove transient and empty-receipt recovery, input/activity/close ordering, back-to-back turn boundaries, completed and failed terminal convergence, stale-binding retention, cross-session progress, non-blocking runtime completion, and restart/reconnect recovery using transport fakes, a shared in-memory store, and fake timers.

Outbox unit coverage proves serialized/coalesced persistence, matching-receipt acknowledgement for content events, timeout retry, concurrent kick idempotency, stop/restart behavior, store failure readiness, and ambiguous-response at-least-once replay without asserting exactly-once Server persistence.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/runner` and `npm test -w packages/runner` pass and leave no Git-visible generated changes.
tasks.output: Shared AgentSession runtime-event outbox and lifecycle in `packages/runner/src`, Workflow reporter integration for durable input/activity/close delivery, receipt-aware ServerConnection methods, and focused in-memory/fake-time runner coverage.
tasks.notes: Implement design decisions D1-D5 and D7 for the Workflow slice. Keep one host-owned outbox and one centralized policy selector; do not send local record IDs to the Server, await network delivery from the Action, claim crash recovery before local commit, key ordering by physical runtime ID, retarget stale records, or retain the reporter's 30-second network settle path. This task is independently usable: Workflow Session transcripts and terminal state recover after upload failure and runner restart while the existing follow-up terminal outbox can remain temporarily until T-002 migrates it.

tasks.title: Deliver follow-up events through the shared outbox
tasks.description: Move Workflow and generic follow-up `session.input` plus operation-correlated completed/failed outcomes onto T-001's shared outbox, preserving input-before-outcome order without coupling retries to runtime invocation. Idempotently import legacy `followup-failures.json` records into the new format, remove the competing terminal-only delivery path, and retain restart-safe delivery for existing pending outcomes.
acceptanceCriteria: The follow-up handler durably enqueues `session.input` with its original discriminated Session target, `runtimeSessionId`, user text, source/kind/role fields, timestamp, and operation ID when present before invoking `runtime.followup`; local enqueue failure returns `unavailable` and invokes no runtime prompt.

After local input persistence succeeds, follow-up HTTP failure, timeout, empty receipt, or server disconnection does not reject the runtime invocation, wait for Server delivery, or invoke the prompt more than once; later retry makes the original input visible when positively accepted.

Operation-correlated `session.followup_completed` and `session.followup_failed` outcomes enter the same logical Session FIFO after input, preserve status/error/completion fields, carry the `successful-response` acknowledgement policy, and remain independently pending on timeout, transport error, non-2xx, or malformed response.

If the Server applies a follow-up terminal outcome but its response is lost, a replayed 2xx with a valid empty receipt array settles the local terminal record and advances the Session queue; matching receipts remain mandatory for follow-up input and all Workflow content/close records.

Workflow and generic follow-up targets use the same outbox route selection and receipt acknowledgement policy; stale physical bindings remain attached to their original records and do not block unrelated Session queues.

On first load, each valid version-1 `.mohist/runner-state/followup-failures.json` entry is mapped to the equivalent `successful-response` terminal event with deterministic ID `legacy-followup-terminal:{operationId}`, merged by ID, and persisted in the new snapshot before the legacy file is marked migrated.

A simulated crash at each migration boundary followed by another load produces one pending record per legacy operation and loses none; invalid or unreadable legacy/new state makes delivery unavailable rather than silently discarding facts or reverting to fire-and-forget behavior.

`FollowupFailureOutbox` and its direct/fire-and-forget event emission paths are removed after migration, and RunnerHost/RunnerSignalRClient use only the shared outbox for follow-up input and terminal lifecycle delivery.

Focused follow-up specs cover Workflow and generic targets, local input persistence failure with no runtime invocation, Server input failure with exactly one runtime invocation, input/outcome ordering, dual delivery failure, empty content receipts, empty terminal replay receipts, restart/reconnect recovery, and retry isolation using the recording filesystem and fake timers only.

RunnerSignalR follow-up specs prove initial and later outbox unhealthiness returns `unavailable` before runtime invocation, restored health permits a later command, and pending delivery/reconnect handling remains active while new commands are gated.

Legacy migration tests run the real snapshot/import store over the recording filesystem and inject failure before new snapshot write, before rename, and before legacy marker; reconstruction produces one record per operation with correct acknowledgement policy and no lost terminal fact.

The obsolete real-filesystem `FollowupFailureOutbox` test is replaced, not duplicated, and existing follow-up command acceptance, unavailable/missing runtime behavior, and terminal outcome regressions remain green.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/runner` and `npm test -w packages/runner` pass and leave no Git-visible generated changes.
tasks.output: Follow-up input and terminal delivery through the shared AgentSession outbox, idempotent legacy terminal-state migration, removal of `FollowupFailureOutbox`, and focused Workflow/generic follow-up recovery tests.
tasks.notes: Consumes T-001's outbox, lifecycle, target-key, and receipt contracts; do not add a second queue or retry `runtime.followup`. Pairwise dependency analysis: T-002 consumes T-001, T-001 consumes no task output, priorities are strictly ordered (1 then 2), and the resulting graph T-001 -> T-002 is acyclic. Preserve new-format pending state during rollback; an older runner cannot deliver newly queued Workflow/input records.
